The reported Gobius paganellus identification is a high-priority voucher/taxonomy check: the Catalog of Fishes lists its distribution in the eastern Atlantic, Mediterranean, Black Sea, southern North Sea and Red Sea, not the Philippines; the paper gives no accession number for a validating specimen.
The abstract and methods give different start months for fish fieldwork. Species totals/frequency terminology should be verified against primary specimen records.

Larval/fry sampling described near the Pansipit mouth took place in Balayan Bay, 10-15 m from shore. Those samples are kept separate from Pansipit River and the estuary absent a precise capture locality.

A separate 2026 cross-check records 21 exact accepted CoL XR matches, one variant match and one synonym match; these are name-match proposals only. The paper attributes several marine taxa at station 5 to high tides in Lingayen; do not classify its pooled list as uniformly freshwater.
Table spelling and author-year discrepancies are recorded in the separate taxonomy cross-check; matching does not verify specimen identity.
Zero current-presence, diet, legal, safety, access or public app assertions are admitted by this source review.

GBIF CoL XR matching is nomenclatural only. Sarotherodon melatheron is a variant match, Cyprinus carpio has a likely author-year typo, and Moolgarda pedaraki has unresolved current-status disagreement across authorities.

Diversity, abundance, and local use of fishes in Lake Danao, Ormoc City, Philippines. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 30(2), 277-288. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/30.2.2023-0009

access.status: Official NFRDI journal and repository records plus the official article PDF's indexed full-text extraction were reviewed. The paper reports fisher-catch sampling twice monthly over 14 months in March-September 2021 and December 2021-June 2022, with a separate 21-fisher interview on 29-30 July 2022. The PDF was not stored locally and its tables were not visually inspected.

reuse.metadata: Citation, study scope and concise, attributed source-reported taxon/evidence notes retained for internal research review.
reuse.raw: No paper PDF, table image, photograph, extended prose or voucher image copied into the repository.
reuse.content: The final article page and journal policy identify CC BY-NC 4.0. Attribution and noncommercial limits apply; this does not approve publication in Bangwit or establish that future project use remains noncommercial.

sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0, stated on the article PDF and in the journal policy
caveats: The combined eight-taxon list draws from fisher catch and a 21-person non-probability interview; Table 2 records only five taxa in fishers' catches, totaling 1,462 individuals. Do not label all eight as specimen-caught in the study.

A 2021 conference abstract reports four taxa and 475 fish during a period nested within the later paper's sampling window. Author overlap and timing indicate possible shared project/data, but no sample-level crosswalk proves independence or exact overlap; never add these totals as separate evidence.

Names, native/introduced status, introduction years, local names and gear associations are transcribed as the authors report them. They have not been independently taxonomically or historically validated; the paper's table and narrative give different introduction timelines for Oreochromis niloticus.

The study is based on subsistence fishers' daily catches and interviews, not standardized effort across all lake habitats. It does not establish current occupancy, lake-wide abundance, complete species coverage or catchability.
The article's Lake Danao coordinates are a study-area locator, not species-specific stations; the datum is not stated and no point or lake geometry is generated.

Diet discussion for Glossogobius giuris and Cyprinus carpio includes cited literature and/or fisher observations; it is not a dedicated local diet study and is not approved as a Bangwit diet or bait recommendation.
The article's CC BY-NC 4.0 terms restrict reuse to attributed noncommercial purposes. No Bangwit publication approval or commercial-use right is established.

sources.title: Fish Composition and Distribution in the Rivers of Lawaan, Eastern Samar, Philippines
sources.provider: Jonh Rey L. Gacura, author-uploaded poster; University of the Philippines Visayas Tacloban College; hosted by ResearchGate
sources.role: Historical source lead for fish sampling in Poblacion and Bolusao Rivers, Lawaan. Poster reports 41 and 15 species by river; a separate project-summary cross-check found 23 and 45 fish aggregates with unresolved scope/date relationships. Extracted poster text exposes a partial table with at least 32 distinct taxon strings; no visually verified complete site/reach/voucher crosswalk; research-only.

access.status: Reviewed the ResearchGate page and its extracted author-uploaded poster text. At least 32 distinct table taxon strings are visible, but the abstract reports 41 Poblacion and 15 Bolusao species. Direct PDF and preview retrieval were blocked, the layout was not visually verified, and the UP Libraries TUKLAS record could not be independently opened.

reuse.metadata: Citation metadata and a short source-bounded summary retained with attribution.
reuse.raw: No poster image, full species list, table, or figure copied. Only the bounded aggregate discrepancy and retrieval limitations were recorded.
reuse.content: ResearchGate warns that content may be subject to copyright; no item-specific derivative-data permission identified.

sources.license: No open license or item-specific reuse permission identified; page warns content may be subject to copyright
caveats: Only Poblacion and Bolusao Rivers were sampled; the poster says Lawaan has seven river systems.
The poster provides richness values of 41 and 15 by river but no confirmed unique combined count; do not add them.

Separate project summaries report 23 and 45 fish species for Lawaan freshwater systems; their relationship to these river-level values is unresolved. See national-visayas-eastern-samar-lawaan-fish-count-crosswalk-20261030.json.

Extracted poster text exposes at least 32 distinct table taxon strings, but the table's completeness and river assignments cannot be visually checked and the names do not reconcile to the abstract totals.
No station geometry, water salinity, complete species-by-river-by-reach list, or voucher crosswalk is verified.
No current presence, freshwater-only classification, catchability, safety, legal, or diet claim is approved for the app.
